newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Poll shows one-fifth of Irish electorate undecided.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows one-fifth of Irish electorate undecided.

text.p: One-fifth of the Irish electorate are undecided about how they will vote at the next general election, due sometime in 1997, an opinion poll said on Tuesday.
The level of undecided voters, which was up eight points at 22 percent since June, has reached pre-election campaign proportions, the Irish Times/MRBI poll showed.
The "new" undecided are largely under the age of 35 years, are mostly women and middle-class, the poll said.
Support for the main opposition party Fianna Fail has dropped by four percentage points to 36 percent over the summer.

Within the ruling coalition support for Fine Gael dropped three points to 20 percent, the Labour party edged up two points in the opinion polls to 10 percent while Democratic Left gained a single point to two percent.
In the popularity stakes opposition leader, Fianna Fail's Bertie Ahern dropped five percentage points to 51 percent.

Coalition party leader Fine Gael's John Bruton lost two points to 54 percent, deputy prime minister and Labour party leader Dick Spring dropped one point to 51 percent while Proinsias De Rossa of Democratic Left enjoyed a two points increase in support to 43 percent.
The poll was conducted among a national quota sample of 1,000 voters at 100 sampling points throughout all constituencies in Ireland last Tuesday and Wednesday.
